walkthroughs.body_html:
The orthodox view dominated in the West for decades.

It says Stalin broke the Yalta agreement, used salami tactics to seize Eastern Europe, and blockaded Berlin. The USA only acted to contain Soviet aggression.

From the 1960s revisionist historians argued the USA was to blame.

They point to the atomic bomb, the Marshall Plan as economic empire-building, and Truman's tough talk at Potsdam. Stalin, they say, only wanted security after losing 27 million in WWII.

Most historians now take a post-revisionist view.

Both sides genuinely feared each other. The Long Telegram and Novikov Telegram show mirror-image suspicions. Ideology and misreading each other's motives made conflict almost certain.
